summary: Kittitas Co., WA site on Table Mountain: 40-ft L-4 built 1932, replaced 1948, gone by 1967; one footing reported left; drive-up with dispersed camping.

facts.design: 40-foot pole L-4 tower (1932), replaced by a new 40-foot L-4 tower in 1948
facts.status_note: Sources disagree on whether the tower was removed or destroyed in 1967. An undated WillhiteWeb photo caption reads 'One footing left'.

staffing.status: Earl Johnson listed as lookout-fireman in June 1933; no later staffing named in the sources read

access.note: Drive-up site with good gravel access, a small campground below the summit and dispersed camping around it, per WillhiteWeb and The Mountaineers. No current agency closure notice was among the sources read.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The summit is used for dispersed camping.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org says it was removed in 1967; firelookout.com says it was destroyed in 1967. The story gives both wordings and does not pick one.

firetower.org says the first tower's cab was apparently salvaged and moved to Sugarloaf in 1949; firelookout.com says it was apparently moved, with no date; WillhiteWeb says it may have been. The story attributes each wording to its source and keeps the hedges.

notes_for_editor: Build and replacement dates agree across three sources. The 1967 removal is disputed (removed vs destroyed). Access is described from WillhiteWeb and The Mountaineers; no current agency page was read, so the public status is medium confidence. The brief's height (12.2 m, from 40 ft) and agency match the sources. The FFLOS and Mountaineers pages cite the route as Forest Road 35-124. The Forest Service page for the Lion Rock Campground was not fetched, so it is not cited.
